label: rem:quark-antiquark-production-reduction
title: Quark--antiquark production: step-by-step Hecke reduction
html:
Step 0: two colored photons collide. Each photon is the Hecke algebra element \gamma = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1. The derivation uses the 3-term specialization \varphi_{01} = 0.

Step 1: expand the product \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2. Their product NF in H_3(q) yields Hopf link terms L_+ and L_- exclusively from cross-color products.

Quark creation: step-by-step reduction of L_+ \cdot e^-. The positive Hopf link L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 applied to the trefoil e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 reduces to:

  \mathrm{NF}(L_+ \cdot e^-)
  = 
  \sigma_1 +
  hL_+ +
  hL_- +
  h^2e^-

The Hopf link operator L_+ transmutes the trefoil electron into a virtual crossing \sigma_1 plus residual Hopf and trefoil content. The e^- coefficient h^2 is the residual electron. The dominant output \sigma_1 is the hadronic crossing that becomes the up quark. The mirror operator L_- creates an antiquark from the positron channel.

Two independent productions. When two independent colored photon pairs undergo pair creation simultaneously, each produces a quark--antiquark channel. The quark type is determined by the crossing orientation.

Meson formation. When the \mathfrak{u} from production 1 and the \bar{\mathfrak{d}} from production 2 come within Hopf linking distance, they bind via \mathcal{L}_H to form a meson. The remaining \bar{\mathfrak{u}} and \mathfrak{d} either annihilate back to photons or form the antimeson.

Three independent productions \to nucleon. For baryon production, three independent pair creations produce three quark--antiquark pairs. Selecting one quark from each pair gives a quark triple which is confined by the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3.
